Consult Summary:
- Adult patient with several days of constant, worsening lower abdominal pain (8/10) and light vaginal spotting while using a contraceptive implant; plan for in-person exam and immediate pregnancy testing.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Constant lower abdominal pain, midline below the umbilicus, present for a few days; worsening; pain rated 8/10.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea without vomiting; light pink vaginal spotting; slight increase in vaginal discharge (small amount); constipation last week (for ~1 week), improved this week.
- Pertinent negatives: No fever or feeling feverish; no shortness of breath; no shoulder pain; no syncope; eating and drinking OK; no vomiting; no dysuria or urinary pain. Urinary frequency pattern unclear; patient reports drinking a lot.
- Gynecologic/sexual: Last menstrual period approximately 2–3 weeks ago; periods occur but are irregular on implant. Sexually active; last intercourse 4 days ago. Contraception: contraceptive implant (Implanon) in place for ~1 year. Pregnancy test done about 1 month ago; not since onset of current pain.
- Past medical history: Amoxicillin allergy.
- Past surgical/obstetric history: No surgeries reported. No previous pregnancies.
- Medications: Contraceptive implant (Implanon) in situ; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social history: Works as a school teacher. Lives with husband and husband’s family. No recent travel (last travel ~1 year ago). Smoking/alcohol use not clearly documented. Illicit drug use denied.

Impression:
- Undifferentiated lower abdominal pain with light vaginal spotting in a patient using a contraceptive implant; pregnancy status currently unknown. Requires in-person assessment and pregnancy exclusion.

Plan:
- Arrange face-to-face clinic visit for abdominal examination; patient to call support line to book.
- Perform a urine pregnancy test today. If positive, contact clinic immediately for urgent evaluation.
- Safety net: Seek earlier care if pain worsens significantly or if unable to keep fluids down.
- Follow-up: Proceed based on in-person examination findings and pregnancy test result.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - Full medication reconciliation (only contraceptive implant documented).
  - Allergy details (type of reaction to amoxicillin not documented).
  - Vitals and physical examination not performed.
  - Detailed urinary symptoms (frequency/urgency/hematuria) not fully clarified.
  - STI risk assessment not documented.
  - Smoking and alcohol use unclear.
● Internal conflicts:
  - Age stated as “23 years,” DOB given as 1996 (potential inconsistency).
  - Response to question about weight loss or blood in stool/urine was unclear; patient redirected to discharge/pain.
● Transcript quality:
  - Several inaudible/unclear segments and interruptions; some answers ambiguous.
